exam: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2004 (28-03-2004)
q: Which of the following is/are a source of Vitamin K?
explanation:
APPSC 2004 key: nuts, eggs, liver. Strictly, green leafy vegetables are the richest source of vitamin K (PMF General Science Part 3 p.14), but option (c) adds tomatoes and carrots, which are poor sources.
Nuts, eggs and animal liver supply vitamin K, which is the exam key. Green leafy vegetables are the best-known source, but tomatoes and carrots are poor, so option (c) is not a clean answer; shark-liver oil gives vitamins A and D.

exam: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2003
q: Which mineral element is present in Vitamin B-12?
explanation: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) contains cobalt; iron is in haemoglobin, magnesium in chlorophyll.

exam: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
q: In which season Vitamin A is required in higher quantities?
explanation:
Official key: Winter. Strictly no authority gives a season-dependent vitamin A requirement for humans ('No seasonal dependence'); deficiency peaks in the hot pre-harvest season (NERC/Cambridge study on India).
The APPSC 2017 key is winter (option A in the paper as printed in Vijeta previous papers). No nutrition authority gives a season-specific vitamin A requirement: ICMR-NIN RDAs depend on age and life stage only.

exam: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
q:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The Haber process is an industrial method used to produce ammonia by reacting nitrogen and hydrogen gases under high temperature and pressure in the presence of an iron catalyst.
Statement II: The Contact process is an important industrial method used to manufacture sulphuric acid, which involves the catalytic oxidation of sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide using vanadium pentoxide (V2O5) as a catalyst.
options: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
key_text: Both statement I and statement II are true.
explanation: Both are true: the Haber process makes ammonia from N2 and H2 over an iron catalyst, and the Contact process makes sulphuric acid by oxidising SO2 to SO3 over V2O5.

exam: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
q: Planets revolve around the sun due to gravitational force. Similarly, electrons revolve around the nucleus due to ____.
explanation: Electrons are held in orbit round the positive nucleus by electrostatic (Coulomb) attraction, just as gravity keeps planets round the Sun.

exam: APPSC Group-II 2011
q: Which of the following has the same atomic number and atomic weight?
explanation: Ordinary hydrogen (protium) has one proton and no neutron, so its atomic number and mass number are both 1; helium is 2 and 4.

exam: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies

exam: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017

explanation: Hydrogen is lighter than air but highly inflammable, so it is the least safe gas for a balloon; helium is inert and safe.

A fat and a strong base

explanation: Gold is the most malleable (and ductile) metal; it can be beaten into leaves a few atoms thick. Silver is next; aluminium and iron are far less malleable.
